decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:01 Rev D02 Rev A03 Rev CEIRFC E2EIRFC S14EIRFC S15EIRFC S7EIRFC S12EIRFC S8EIRFC S9EIRFC S10EIRFC S11EIRFC S1EIRFC S6EIRFC S2EIRFC S3EIRFC S4EIRFC S5EIRFC S13EIRFC T1EIRFC S16EIRFC L1Planning Design and Access Statement Rev FPreliminary Ecological AppraisalLighting Assessment Dated 17.08.2026Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a tree survey and a scheme for the protection of all trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall cover all stages of the development, including preparatory work, construction and landscaping. The scheme shall comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures. Multiple TPPs may be necessary to demonstrate tree protection throughout the various stages of the development.Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a) All required tree works;b) the finalised location and installation methodology of all electricity supply apparatus, utility services/drainage, seeking to avoid the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retained trees (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);c) any removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;d) details of any construction within RPAs;e) a full specification for the construction of any paths or other hard surfacing (including alterations to the existing layout of internal roads and hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;f) detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;g) a full specification for the installation of any boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;h) a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during preparation, construction and landscaping phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;i) a specification for ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);j) details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;k) a detailed schedule of arboricultural supervision for checking tree protection measures at intervals through the project, and for overseeing any works within RPAs which are unavoidable.The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Should any of the above not be applicable to this development, this shall be stated in the AMS.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990

The floodlighting hereby approved shall be installed and thereafter retained in accordance with the approved lighting design, including the approved aiming angles, luminaire positions, shielding and louvre arrangements. No alterations shall be made to the approved specification unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To minimise light spill and protect biodiversity interests in the vicinity of the site.

The floodlighting hereby approved shall only be operated between 12:30 and 21:30 hours Monday to Saturday and 12:30 to 17:00 on Sunday and shall be switched off outside these hours. Between the end of sporting activities and final switch-off, the lighting shall operate only at a dimmed level in accordance with the approved lighting strategy.Reason: To protect biodiversity and safeguard residential amenity.

The floodlighting hereby approved shall only be operated during the rugby season between 1 September and 30 April in any calendar year. Outside this period, the floodlighting shall remain switched off except for maintenance, testing or commissioning purposes.Reason: To minimise impacts on protected species and biodiversity.

No additional lighting, including security lighting, column-mounted lighting, cabinet lighting or pathway lighting, shall be installed within the application site unless otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To prevent unnecessary illumination and protect ecological interests.

The floodlighting shall be installed and thereafter retained using luminaires with a correlated colour temperature of no greater than 4000 Kelvin, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To minimise adverse impacts on bats and other nocturnal wildlife.

The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the Precautionary Working Method Statement contained within Section 9 of the approved Preliminary Ecological Appraisal.Reason: To safeguard biodiversity during the construction phase.
